meta_description: Turn signed B2B SaaS deals into clean customer onboarding with a weekly operating cadence and blocker ownership.
for_whom: For 5-100 person B2B SaaS, AI, infra, and devtools teams with messy post-sale onboarding
hero_headline: Turn signed deals into clean go-lives without dragging founders and engineers into project-manager mode
hero_subheadline: We run the first 2-6 weeks of onboarding: kickoff, milestone tracking, blocker chasing, and customer-ready updates until handoff.
secondary_cta_text: See a sample onboarding status pack
credibility_line: Least-privilege access. Customer-facing updates stay aligned with your team. You approve escalations and scope changes.
pain_paragraph: Most small B2B SaaS teams close the deal, then immediately fall into onboarding chaos: kickoff emails, access requests, blocker chasing, and scattered ownership. Go-lives slip, customers lose confidence, and senior people waste time acting like accidental project managers.
before: Signed deals vanish into Slack threads and scattered checklists
Customers wait days for a clear kickoff and next-step plan
AEs, founders, and engineers keep chasing the same blockers
Nobody can quickly answer: what is blocking this go-live?
after: Every new customer gets a clean kickoff and mutual action plan
One live blocker tracker with owners, deadlines, and escalation rules
Weekly customer-ready status updates without founder babysitting
Faster time-to-value and cleaner handoff into CS/support
offer_summary: GoLive Desk is a done-for-you onboarding operations layer for signed B2B SaaS deals. We run kickoff, maintain the implementation plan, chase blockers on both sides, and keep everyone aligned until the customer is live or cleanly handed off.
included: Kickoff prep, agenda, and first-30-day onboarding plan
Mutual action plan or milestone tracker with named owners
Blocker log with follow-ups and escalation cadence
Weekly internal summary + customer-facing status update draft
Handoff checklist into customer success / support once stable
excluded: Product configuration or custom engineering work
Data migration execution or solution architecture delivery
24/7 support coverage or customer support queue ownership
Commercial negotiation after the deal is signed
process: 15-minute fit call to confirm onboarding volume, motion, and systems
Week 1: collect current checklist, define milestones, and launch kickoff cadence
Weeks 1-6: run blocker follow-ups, status updates, and owner accountability
Handoff: package open items, next steps, and ownership for CS/support
pricing_details: Best for 1-2 active onboardings with a standard weekly cadence. Growth tier: $2,500-$3,000/mo for higher stakeholder complexity or multiple simultaneous onboardings. Pilot option: $500-$750 for kickoff + first-week operating setup.
guarantee_line: If we do not launch your onboarding tracker and first status cadence within 5 business days of a complete handoff, we keep working free until it is live.

faq.a: Usually a shared project tracker, meeting notes, and the customer-facing status thread or inbox. We work with least-privilege access and do not need production credentials.

faq.q: What needs to be true for this to work?
faq.a: You need one named internal owner, one customer-side champion, and a reasonably defined onboarding outcome. If nobody owns the relationship, this turns into chaos no matter who runs the checklist.
Most engagements run 2-6 weeks depending on the customer and integration complexity. We focus on the operating cadence, not the technical implementation itself.

faq.q: How do you handle customer data and retention?
faq.a: We only retain the artifacts needed for active onboarding work, prefer redacted or low-sensitivity materials where possible, and can follow a defined deletion window after handoff.
We get the kickoff moving fast, keep the milestone plan current, chase blockers, and package progress into clear weekly updates so your team and the customer stay aligned.

trust_basics_line: Works best when you already have a real product implementation path but no one cleanly running the onboarding operations layer.
